findings.summary: The new row binding checks only an item's current text. Its proposed text may still contain newlines, so a row-bound item can insert whole new rows into the §5.3 table. Free text in proposed, replacement and residual fields is still accepted; that is by design, since review covers content.
findings.evidence: Probes on scratch copies, with §12 re-rendered and the pin recomputed. findings.summary: The corrected writer route (an ordinary root exec, then a capset drop) gives the empty permitted set the ptrace read needs. It leaves the writer's bounding set as the starter's, though the §5.3 header asks for 'bounding equal' (empty for POLICY_WRITER). Under matrix v4 the writer cannot empty its bounding set itself. This tension predates HS43 and is inert, but worth recording.
findings.evidence: From my own knowledge of v6.12. capset (cap_capset) cannot change the bounding set. PR_CAPBSET_DROP (cap_prctl_drop) needs CAP_SETPCAP, and SELinux then checks 'capability setpcap'. matrix.json grants setpcap only to init_t and qualk8s_runtime_t; planeon_policy_writer_t has no capability grant. The starter (planeon_admin_t) has no setpcap either. A full bounding set with an empty permitted set, no_new_privs and no exec in the writer's filter gains nothing back, so the gap is inert. Suggest one sentence or a carried item: the writer's bounding set stays the starter's, or §5.3's header needs an exception for the writer.

(a) O-MATRIX-GATE-PROCACCESS: 'a reader keeps either all of the gate's entries or none' overstates. Class lnk_file (exe, cwd, root, fd/*) can be withheld separately from class file. But P1 needs the exe link, and environ and maps share class file with stat and status, so the practical conclusion holds. (b) The base-clause replacement says the gate does not authenticate the broker's artifact or manifest/trust custody 'per frame'. H1 says the gate never checks it, so 'per frame' invites reading that it does at the first frame. (c) O-W03-WRITER-EXE: '... which matrix v4 gives READ ..., so the exec grants nothing beyond the starter's own set'. READ is what keeps the exec dumpable (would_dump). 'Grants nothing' comes from a root exec yielding permitted = bounding, within the starter's set. (d) R-GATE-PROC's decisions are Q-HS43-3 and Q-HE2S-7; HS43-GATE-RESIDUAL-CONFIRM, which carries O-MATRIX-GATE-PROCACCESS, is not listed. (e) H1's first bullet gives the kernel preconditions of the broker's read but not its SELinux side (matrix procAccess planeon_broker_t -> planeon_gate_t, 'file read'), which the writer bullet does state.
